title: Adaptive slice staging with manual latch and automated triage hooks
author: Evelyn Chen
release_notes: Adds an adaptive slice staging controller that supports entropy-buffered phased promotes, manual latch points for human-in-the-loop cutovers, and an automated triage integration that opens a rollback playbook when defined SLOs regress.
description: Motivation: Improve safety and speed of multi-variant model promotes by combining staged slice promotions with an operator-controlled latch and automated triage hooks. Many existing rollouts at Redwood rely on timeboxed canaries or heuristic gating; this change introduces a small controller and runtime hooks that let platform teams: (1) define entropy-buffered phase boundaries that vary traffic fraction based on observed signal variance, (2) pause at a manual latch before wide promotion so on-call can inspect telemetry, and (3) automatically run predefined triage playbooks (smoke replay, shadow-replay, differential-bisect dry-run) and trigger rollback when metric thresholds are exceeded. This PR is intended for the model rollout path: it plugs into the servegraph and the rollout orchestrator and is backward compatible with existing promote APIs. Checklist: - [x] Controller implementation + unit tests - [x] E2E smoke harness (local replay driver) - [x] Telemetry alarms and triage hook wiring - [x] Docs (console + runbook) - [x] Upgrade path validated with existing staged promotes Changes in one sentence: Add AdaptiveSliceStaging controller, telemetry-based entropy scaling for phase increments, manual-latch resource, and triage hook integration to trigger automated rollback. Related: ENG-1934 (policy-driven staging), PM-420 (console flow for manual latch). Impact/risk: Moderate (rollout orchestration path). New controller is feature-flagged (rollout.experimental.adaptive_slice) and defaults to disabled in production controlled clusters. Rollout plan: enable feature-flag on staging for one week, run two internal promotes, turn on on dogfooding clusters with manual latch active, then flip to autoscale mode if stable.

patch_snippets:
--- a/runtime/traffic/slice_router.go
+++ b/runtime/traffic/slice_router.go
@@ -45,7 +45,18 @@ func (r *SliceRouter) ApplyFraction(sliceID string, base float64) {
-    // simple linear fraction application
-    r.apply(sliceID, base)
+    // entropy-buffered increment: if signal variance low, increase faster; else slow down
+    variance := r.telemetry.SignalVariance(sliceID)
+    scale := math.Exp(-variance*2.0) // tuned in tests
+    adjusted := base * (0.5 + 0.5*scale)
+    r.apply(sliceID, adjusted)
 }
